explanation: An inverse function undoes the original: whatever f does to x, f⁻¹ reverses it. Geometrically that means swapping every (x, y) into (y, x), which reflects the graph across the dashed line y = x. Slide m and b and watch both lines pivot — the green tie-line shows a point and its mirror image always landing symmetrically across y = x.
bullets: To find an inverse, swap x and y, then solve for y.
f and f⁻¹ are mirror images across the line y = x.
Only one-to-one functions have an inverse (each output from one input).
